summary: The current ParseOffset implementation accepts a one-digit hour because it does not verify that ParseInt consumed both required digits. Valid offsets also produce reversed timestamp shifts, but the supplied excerpt omits the conversion that applies the parsed offset, so its sign convention cannot yet be confirmed for a concrete repair.
hypotheses: ParseOffset accepts one-digit offset hours because it does not require exactly two digits for the hour field.
The parsed offset sign is applied inconsistently with the later civil-time-to-instant conversion, reversing valid offset shifts.
